blogSections.title: Facing Volatility with Innovation
paragraphs: In much of Latin America, managing money often means navigating uncertainty. From currency volatility, high transaction fees and limited access to global financial services, individuals and small businesses face daily challenges in maintaining economic stability.

In this context, crypto is gaining traction not as a trend, but as a tool. Across the region, people are adopting cryptocurrencies, especially stablecoins and digital payment solutions to solve real problems—preserving value during times of volatility, receiving payments from abroad, and accessing digital finance without relying on traditional banking systems.

This shift is especially noticeable in cross-border payments. Traditional channels can be costly and slow, often involving multiple intermediaries. In contrast, crypto offers near-instant transfers, lower fees, and greater accessibility—even for those without a formal bank account.

What we’re seeing in Latin America is not a speculative rush, but a pragmatic transition: from digital assets to real-world utility. From holding crypto to actively using them in daily life. And from barriers to empowerment—powered by technology, and catered to local needs.

blogSections.title: Why Crypto Adoption in LATAM Is Different
paragraphs: Crypto adoption in Latin America is shaped by real-world needs rather than market trends. Unlike regions where crypto is often viewed through the lens of speculation or investment, in LATAM, it serves a more grounded function: offering financial tools where traditional systems fall short.
bullets: In countries with volatile exchange rates, crypto offers a more stable alternative for cross-border payments.
Freelancers and remote workers use stablecoins to receive payments from clients abroad—often faster and with lower fees than traditional methods.
Small businesses adopt crypto to access a broader customer base and reduce exposure to local currency fluctuations.
For many without access to conventional banking, crypto wallets offer a first entry point into global commerce.
paragraphsAfterBullets: In this context, crypto isn’t just a new financial asset—it’s a practical solution for navigating regional challenges. Its adoption continues to grow, not through hype, but through daily utility.

information.title: Managing your Card
information.desc: What if my card expires — can I keep using it? Will it renew automatically?

faqs.question: What if my card expires — can I keep using it? Will it renew automatically?
faqs.answer:
Once your card expires, it can no longer be used, and automatic renewal is not supported.
If your card is expiring soon or already expired, you can apply for a replacement (renewal) in the app under the card's settings.
📌 Be sure to check and update your shipping address before requesting a replacement, as it will default to your previously saved address.

faqs.question: Why did my payment fail with the virtual card?
faqs.answer:
A failed transaction doesn't necessarily mean the card is faulty.
It could be due to several reasons:
▶ The merchant does not accept prepaid or virtual cards
▶ Your card has insufficient balance or no funds transferred in
▶ The card is inactive or past its expiration date
We suggest testing the card on another supported platform and checking the balance status. If issues persist, contact our support team with the transaction details.

faqs.question: How many times can I use this card? Does it expire?
faqs.answer:
NewPay cards are reusable and do not have a swipe limit — as long as there's available balance, you can keep using it.
Each card comes with a fixed expiration date (usually 2–3 years), which you can check in the card details screen.

faqs.question: Why can't I link my card to Apple Pay or Google Pay?
faqs.answer:
We understand how frustrating that can be — linking your card should be quick and easy.
But don’t worry, here are a few common reasons that might be causing the issue:
▶ The card hasn’t been activated or funded yet, please make sure your card is activated in the NEWPAY app and that you've transferred some balance into it.
▶ Some wallets try to make a small verification charge when linking a card — if your balance is zero, the process might fail.
▶ Card details were entered incorrectly.It’s easy to overlook small details. Be sure to double-check your card number, expiration date (MM/YY), and CVV.Even a single wrong digit or formatting issue can stop the card from linking.
▶ Your device or region may not be supported.Make sure your phone’s OS version and region settings are compatible with Apple Pay or Google Pay.Some devices or locations might not support wallet linking yet.
▶ Network issues can interfere. Sometimes the connection just isn’t cooperating. Try switching to a different network or restarting your phone, then attempt to link the card again.
If you’ve gone through all these checks and it’s still not working, feel free to take a screenshot of the error and contact our support team — we’re here to help.

faqs.question: I already have one virtual card — can I get another?
faqs.answer:
Of course, You can apply for multiple cards, but please note that each user can hold up to 5 cards in total, including virtual cards, physical cards, and gift cards.
Once you reach the card limit, it will no longer be possible to apply for new cards, and currently, disabling or deleting existing cards does not free up card slots.
We recommend organizing your existing cards based on different needs to keep things clear and efficient.
If you have any questions, feel free to reach out to us anytime!

faqs.question: Can I use my physical card overseas? Will it be blocked?
faqs.answer:
Yes, definitely! NewPay physical cards support global use in countries and regions where Visa or Mastercard is accepted.
This includes online payments, in-store purchases, and ATM withdrawals.
There are no country restrictions on our end, but please note:
▶ Ensure your card is activated and has sufficient balance
▶ Some regions may have ATM or merchant limitations due to local policies or systems

faqs.question: My card didn’t work at the supermarket — Is there a problem with the card?
faqs.answer:
A failed in-store payment doesn't necessarily mean the card is faulty.
Common reasons for failure include:
▶ The merchant's POS terminal doesn't support your card type or had a read error
▶ Network issues or failure in the acquiring system
▶ The card hasn't been activated or has insufficient balance
▶ The transaction exceeded the card's limit setting
Please check that your card is activated and has enough balance. If the issue continues, try using the card at a different merchant or online. Feel free to contact support for help.

faqs.question: Can I use this card at gas stations or convenience stores?
faqs.answer:
Yes, both NEWPAY virtual and physical cards are compatible with Visa/Mastercard networks worldwide, including at gas stations, convenience stores, supermarkets, restaurants, and e-commerce sites.
Our cards are designed for broad international usability, online and offline.
Please ensure your card is activated and has sufficient balance. Some merchants may require tap-to-pay or chip-insertion terminals.

faqs.question: Why can’t I reactivate my card after deleting my account?
faqs.answer:
Once you delete your NEWPAY account, all cards and data are permanently erased and cannot be recovered or reactivated. This is due to:
▶ Data protection & privacy laws: We must fully erase your ID and account records after deletion
▶ Fraud prevention: We block repeat registrations with the same ID to prevent misuse.
▶ Regulatory compliance: Financial platforms must ensure one identity = one account, with no re-use after deletion.
We recommend you only delete your account if you are certain you no longer need the service. If you simply want a break, you can freeze your cards instead.

information.title: Opening Your Account
information.desc: NewPay App Download, Account Registration, Identity Verification

faqs.question: Register Account
faqs.answer:
Visit the NEWPAY official website or download the NEWPAY app.
Click "Sign Up" and fill in the following information:
Email address
Enter the Invitation Code (User UID)
Read and agree to the Registration Agreement.
Submit your registration by clicking "Next".
Complete email or SMS code verification.
Set your login password.

faqs.question: What features do I get after completing KYC? Is it really required?
faqs.answer:
Completing KYC unlocks all of NEWPAY’s features, including:
Virtual and physical card activation/Gift card use/Transactions,/withdrawals/statements.
KYC is mandatory for security, regulatory compliance, and fraud prevention. We appreciate your cooperation in helping us maintain a safe environment.

faqs.question: My KYC got rejected and I didn’t even get a reason. How do I fix it?
faqs.answer:
We understand it can be frustrating. However, due to anti-fraud and compliance design, the system may not disclose specific rejection reasons.
When resubmitting your documents, please make sure:
♦ The ID photo is clear, unobstructed, and shows all corners
♦ You're using a valid, government-issued ID from a supported region
♦ For address verification, submit a document that clearly shows your full name and residential address
♦ Avoid uploading screenshots, filtered photos, or edited images
If everything looks good but it still fails, please contact support for help with resubmission.

faqs.question: The system says my photo is blurry, but it looks fine to me.
faqs.answer:
While the image may appear clear to the human eye, our system uses automated image recognition, which may detect issues not visible to you.
You may get this error if:
♦ The image is slightly blurry, has glare, shadows, or is missing corners
♦ The file size exceeds 20MB and fails to upload
♦  The image resolution is too low or compressed
♦ Make sure the file is clear, unedited, glare-free, and under the size limit.
These requirements ensure we meet international KYC compliance standards.

faqs.question: Email/Phone Verification Guide
faqs.answer:
Verification Process:
1.Upon registration, the system will automatically send a verification email or SMS code.
2.Complete the binding process by clicking the verification link in the email or entering the SMS code.
3.If you do not receive the verification code, you may:
ㅤ3.1 Check your spam or junk folder, or SMS filtering settings.
ㅤ3.2 Request a resend of the verification email or SMS.
ㅤ3.3 Contact customer support for further assistance.

information.title: Managing Your Transaction
information.desc: Card Transactions, ATM Withdrawals, Payment Settings, Refunds, PayPal Transfers, Card Fraud, Bill statement

faqs.question: My transaction keeps saying‘Pending.’Has the money been taken?
faqs.answer:
When a transaction is marked“Pending,” it means the merchant requested authorization, but the charge hasn’t been finalized yet.
This amount is temporarily held but won’t be deducted until the merchant completes the settlement process.
This usually takes 1–5 business days, depending on the merchant, bank, and holidays.
Please be patient — your app will update automatically once it’s completed.

faqs.question: My payment failed but money was still deducted — will I get it back?
faqs.answer:
Some failed transactions may appear as charged because of pre-authorization holds, which are used to verify transaction intent.
If the transaction ultimately fails, the hold will not be settled and will be automatically released back to your account.
This typically happens within 1–7 business days, depending on the merchant and settlement channel.

faqs.question: Why did my card binding fail during subscription setup?
faqs.answer:
Some merchants apply strict verification rules. Certain platforms may perform a small pre-authorization charge or require support for recurring payments. If the card doesn’t meet these technical requirements, the binding may fail.
Additionally, even if the first subscription appears free, many platforms may still attempt a small verification charge. If your card has insufficient balance, the verification may fail and prevent successful binding.
Lastly, some platforms only accept cards issued in specific regions, which may exclude NewPay cards depending on the merchant’s supported list.

faqs.question: I got a refund but the money doesn’t show up in the app yet. Why?
faqs.answer:
Refunds must be initiated by the merchant and returned through the same channel.
NewPay can only reflect the refund after we’ve received the funds from the merchant.
Depending on the payment gateway and merchant, refunds usually take 3–10 business days.
If it’s been longer than expected, feel free to contact our support team with refund details.

faqs.question: Can I download my transaction history or a billing report?
faqs.answer:
Yes! You can export transaction history within a custom date range in the app for bookkeeping or review.
Also, NewPay automatically sends a monthly statement to your registered email after each billing cycle.

faqs.question: I paid online but the page didn’t finish loading — was it charged?
faqs.answer:
If the payment page didn’t redirect or complete, it doesn’t always mean the transaction succeeded or failed.Here’s what you should do:
Check the [Transaction History] in the NewPay app to confirm if a payment was recorded.
Log in to the merchant’s platform to see if the order was created or marked as paid.
Make sure your network is stable when making payments to avoid errors or duplicate attempts

faqs.question: Can I pay in installments when spending?
faqs.answer:
NewPay cards are prepaid, not credit cards — so installment payments aren't supported.
All purchases are charged based on the available balance on your card. If there isn't enough to cover the full amount, the payment will fail.
We recommend checking your card balance before making large purchases.

faqs.question: Do I get notified after each payment?
faqs.answer:
Yes, NewPay sends instant alerts via app notifications whenever you make a payment.
To stay informed of your spending activity, please make sure app notifications are enabled on your device.

information.title: Deposit and Withdrawal
information.desc: Deposit and Withdrawal Process, Frequently Asked Questions for Deposit and Withdrawal

faqs.question: My wallet shows the transfer as successful, but I don’t see it in the app. Is it stuck?
faqs.answer:
“Transfer successful” in your wallet means the transaction was sent to the blockchain — but it still needs to be confirmed and synced with NEWPAY.
Typically, this takes 1–10 minutes depending on the network.
If it’s been over 15 minutes, please check:
Did you choose the same network (ERC20/TRC20) as shown on our page?
Did you send it to the exact address displayed in your NEWPAY recharge screen?
Did you meet the minimum recharge amount?
If everything checks out, please contact support and provide the transaction hash (TXID) for assistance.

faqs.question: Why is the deposit address different every time? Can’t I reuse the old one?
faqs.answer:
For security reasons, we use dynamic deposit addresses to prevent address tampering, leaking, or repeated accidental transfers.
Always use the latest address shown on the payment page. Please don’t reuse previous addresses to avoid any issues.

faqs.question: I just sent USDT, why hasn't it arrived yet?
faqs.answer:
Blockchain networks sometimes get congested, causing a delay in transaction confirmation.
Since USDT is a blockchain-based asset, the arrival time depends on the network you used (like TRC20 or ERC20), miner fees, and network traffic.

faqs.question: I withdrew USDT to my wallet, but it hasn’t arrived.
faqs.answer:
Once your withdrawal request is submitted, it enters the blockchain network for confirmation.
Transfer times can vary depending on network congestion — especially during peak periods.

faqs.question: Why do I have to enable 2FA when withdrawing?
faqs.answer:
To protect your account and funds, NEWPAY requires Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) for withdrawals and other sensitive actions.
Even if someone knows your password, 2FA helps prevent unauthorized access to your money.
We recommend using the Google Authenticator app — setup takes just a few minutes and greatly improves your security.

faqs.question: My physical card has money, but the ATM says the balance is 0?
faqs.answer:
The balance shown at an ATM refers to the card balance, not your main account balance in the NEWPAY app.
There are two common cases:
Case 1: Funds already transferred to the card
→ Don’t worry — even if the ATM says 0, you can still withdraw if your card has sufficient balance. Some ATM systems simply don’t sync the balance correctly but the withdrawal still works.
Case 2: Funds are still in your main account, not on the card
→ Go to the NEWPAY app → [Card] section → Select your physical card → Tap [Transfer In] to load funds onto the card, then try again at the ATM.

faqs.question: My withdrawal show ‘processing/in progress’ — it already been deducted?
faqs.answer:
When your withdrawal status shows “Processing” or “In Progress,” it means your request is under review or being prepared for blockchain submission.
At this point, your funds are not yet deducted.
Once the transaction is approved and sent to the blockchain, the status will change to “Completed.”
If a transaction fails due to address issues or risk flags, it will be automatically canceled and the funds returned.

faqs.question: Can I cancel a withdrawal after submitting it?
faqs.answer:
Once a withdrawal has been submitted and passes internal checks, it will be broadcast to the blockchain (e.g., ERC20 or TRC20).
Since blockchain transactions are irreversible, they cannot be modified, canceled, or refunded after submission — by you or by us.
This is different from traditional bank systems, which sometimes allow reversals.
📌 Please always double-check the address, network, and amount before submitting to avoid irreversible loss.

faqs.question: Can I withdraw directly to my bank account?
faqs.answer:
Currently, NEWPAY doesn’t support direct withdrawals to bank accounts.
Instead, you can withdraw in two ways:
Withdraw USDT to a personal crypto wallet.
→ Network fee applies (gas fee), determined by blockchain, not NEWPAY
Withdraw cash using a physical card at ATMs
 → 2% withdrawal fee + applicable foreign exchange rate (based on bank rates)

faqs.question: Account Security
faqs.answer:
Protecting your account credentials is the first step toward ensuring the safety of your funds.
▲ Never share your login credentials
Do not share your login email, password, or verification codes with anyone — not even NewPay staff. If you receive any suspicious requests, report them to us immediately.
▲ Enable Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)
Strengthen your account security by enabling 2FA. This adds an additional layer of protection by requiring a one-time code when logging in. You can activate this feature in Settings > Security Settings within the NewPay app.
▲ Do not reuse your NewPay password on other platforms
Use a strong, unique password for your NewPay account. Reusing passwords across platforms increases your exposure to credential breaches and potential fraud.

faqs.question: Official Access & Scam Prevention
faqs.answer:
Always access NewPay through official channels and stay alert to phishing or impersonation attempts.
▲Only use the official NewPay app and website
Download the NewPay app exclusively from the App Store or Google Play, and access services through our official website: www.newpay.org. Avoid clicking on unknown links or scanning unverified QR codes.
▲Be cautious of scam messages and fake support accounts
NewPay will never contact you via private messages on social media to request personal information. If you encounter suspicious accounts claiming to represent NewPay, do not engage and report them to us.

faqs.question: Device & Network Safety
faqs.answer:
Use secure devices and networks to prevent unauthorized access and data interception.
▲ Avoid logging in through public Wi-Fi
Public networks can expose your data to malicious interception. Always log in to NewPay from a secure, trusted network — especially when performing sensitive actions like transfers or withdrawals.
▲ Keep your app up to date
Ensure you are using the latest version of the NewPay app to benefit from security patches and performance improvements. Updates often include critical fixes that protect you from emerging threats.

faqs.question: Card & Transaction Safety
faqs.answer:
Monitoring your card activity regularly helps detect and prevent unauthorized transactions.
▲Freeze your card if you notice suspicious activity
If you detect any unfamiliar transactions, use the in-app freeze function to instantly block your card and prevent further use. Then contact our support team for assistance.
▲Review your transaction history frequently
We recommend checking your transaction records on a weekly basis to verify all activity. If you notice anything unusual, report it to us promptly.

faqs.question: Account Deletion Notice
faqs.answer:
Please think carefully before deleting your account — this action is permanent and irreversible.
▲ Account deletion is permanent and non-reversible
Once your account is deleted, all associated cards, data, and history will be permanently erased and cannot be recovered. This policy complies with data protection regulations and anti-fraud protocols.
▲ Consider freezing your account or cards instead
If you’re only taking a temporary break, we recommend using the card freeze feature instead of deleting your account. This allows you to retain your account and resume usage later if needed.

topArticles.question: I already have one virtual card — can I get another?
topArticles.answer:
Of course, You can apply for multiple cards, but please note that each user can hold up to 5 cards in total, including virtual cards, physical cards, and gift cards.
Once you reach the card limit, it will no longer be possible to apply for new cards, and currently, disabling or deleting existing cards does not free up card slots.
We recommend organizing your existing cards based on different needs to keep things clear and efficient.
If you have any questions, feel free to reach out to us anytime!

topArticles.question: Why do I have to enable 2FA when withdrawing?
topArticles.answer:
To protect your account and funds, NEWPAY requires Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) for withdrawals and other sensitive actions.
Even if someone knows your password, 2FA helps prevent unauthorized access to your money.
We recommend using the Google Authenticator app — setup takes just a few minutes and greatly improves your security.

topArticles.question: Register Account
topArticles.answer:
Visit the NEWPAY official website or download the NEWPAY app.
Click "Sign Up" and fill in the following information:
Email address
Enter the Invitation Code (User UID)
Read and agree to the Registration Agreement.
Submit your registration by clicking "Next".
Complete email or SMS code verification.
Set your login password.

topArticles.question: Official Access & Scam Prevention
topArticles.answer:
Always access NewPay through official channels and stay alert to phishing or impersonation attempts.
▲Only use the official NewPay app and website
Download the NewPay app exclusively from the App Store or Google Play, and access services through our official website: www.newpay.org. Avoid clicking on unknown links or scanning unverified QR codes.
▲Be cautious of scam messages and fake support accounts
NewPay will never contact you via private messages on social media to request personal information. If you encounter suspicious accounts claiming to represent NewPay, do not engage and report them to us.

topArticles.question: Can I pay in installments when spending?
topArticles.answer:
NewPay cards are prepaid, not credit cards — so installment payments aren't supported.
All purchases are charged based on the available balance on your card. If there isn't enough to cover the full amount, the payment will fail.
We recommend checking your card balance before making large purchases.
